The Hotel shall ensure adequate staffing to provide professional service, but the Hotel's determination of adequate staffing levels shall not be subject to challenge by the Group and shall be final.
findings.headline: No guaranteed server or bartender ratios
findings.finding_text: Staffing is entirely discretionary and unchallengeable, so service levels are not guaranteed.
findings.cd_standard: Minimum ratios: 1 server per 25 (plated breakfast), 20 (plated lunch/dinner), 40/30 for buffets; 1 bartender per 75 hosted, 100 cash.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner. At all functions where alcohol is served, Hotel will provide no fewer than one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars.
findings.redline_note: Minimum server and bartender ratios are guaranteed.
findings.compromise_range: Staffing ratios up to 20% looser than the standard, e.g. one server per 30 guests at plated breakfasts.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel charges labor and bartender fees on Group's food and beverage functions, calculated on the basis of estimated attendance, the scope of service, and the Hotel's then-current labor rates, which fees shall be itemized separately on the Group's invoice and shall be payable as part of the total food and beverage charges due under this Agreement.
findings.headline: Labor and bartender fees charged on all functions
findings.finding_text: Fees apply to every function at then-current rates, on top of the 24% service charge.
findings.cd_standard: No labor, bartender or service fees except a $150 labor fee for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: There will be no special labor, bartender, or service fees for any Group food or beverage function, except that functions of fewer than twenty-five (25) people will incur a labor fee of $150.
findings.redline_note: Labor fees apply only to functions under twenty-five people.
findings.compromise_range: Staffing ratios up to 20% looser than the standard, e.g. one server per 30 guests at plated breakfasts.

findings.quoted_text: Labor fees shall include compensation for all service staff, supervisory personnel, and setup and breakdown labor, and the Group shall have no right to engage outside service providers or to reduce these fees by providing its own staff.
findings.headline: Group cannot reduce labor fees or use own staff
findings.finding_text: The group is locked into the Hotel's labor fees with no ability to avoid them.
findings.cd_standard: No labor fees for meeting ratios, except for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: Labor fees are limited to the fee for functions of fewer than twenty-five (25) people as set out in this Agreement.
findings.redline_note: Labor fees are limited to the stated small-function fee.
findings.compromise_range: Staffing ratios up to 20% looser than the standard, e.g. one server per 30 guests at plated breakfasts.

findings.quoted_text: The Group shall have no entitlement to pricing quoted prior to the date of this Agreement, and any quotation for audio-visual or internet services shall be deemed valid only for the date on which it was provided. The Hotel reserves the right to adjust pricing for audio-visual equipment, technical support, bandwidth, and all related services up to the time of the Event.
findings.headline: AV and internet quotes not honored; prices adjustable
findings.finding_text: Quoted pricing is not locked and no bandwidth minimum or discount for additions is stated.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel honors attached AV and internet quotes (min. 10 Mbps down / 1 Mbps up) with a 20% discount on additions.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote, prepared from Group's specifications at the time of contracting, and will apply a discount of twenty percent (20%) to any additional audio-visual needs, regardless of which provider is in place during the Event. Hotel will likewise honor the attached internet bandwidth quote, which provides a minimum of 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload speed, with a discount of twenty percent (20%) on any additional needs.

findings.quoted_text: Complimentary internet access and any discounted or complimentary services relating to audio-visual provision, including concessions, upgrades, or technical support at no charge, shall be conditioned upon the Group's exclusive use of the Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider for all function space during the Event. Should the Group elect to contract with an outside audio-visual vendor or bring its own equipment into any function room, the Group shall forfeit all complimentary internet services, discounted rates, and any other concessions the Hotel has offered in connection with in-house provision, and the Group shall pay the Hotel's then-current rate for internet access and technical support.
findings.headline: Complimentary services conditioned on exclusive in-house AV
findings.finding_text: Using an outside AV vendor forfeits internet and all other concessions.
findings.cd_standard: Using the in-house AV provider is never a condition for discounted or complimentary services such as internet.
findings.proposed_language: Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider, exclusively or otherwise, will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, such as internet.

findings.quoted_text: Hotel's consent to any proposed assignment is entirely within Hotel's sole discretion and may be withheld in Hotel's absolute discretion for any reason whatsoever, or for no reason at all.
findings.headline: Hotel may refuse any assignment for any reason
findings.finding_text: The group cannot move the contract to a successor management company or affiliate without the Hotel's agreement, and the Hotel need not give reasons. Silence from the Hotel is not approval, and the group stays liable even after an approved assignment.
findings.cd_standard: The group should be able to assign the contract to a successor management company or affiliated entity (common for associations that rotate management) without the hotel's consent being unreasonably withheld, particularly where the event itself is unchanged.

findings.quoted_text: This indemnification obligation shall extend to claims arising from the Hotel's own negligence in its provision of services or maintenance of premises, provided that Group's indemnity shall not extend to claims arising solely from the Hotel's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
findings.headline: Group indemnifies Hotel for the Hotel's own negligence
findings.finding_text: The group would cover losses caused by the Hotel's negligence, except gross negligence or willful misconduct. This could expose the group to large third-party claims for conditions it did not create.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual and limited to each party's own negligence or willful misconduct, including each party's reasonable attorney's fees, and should survive the end of the agreement — the group should never indemnify the hotel for the hotel's own negligence. Insurance should be a mutual obligation, with each party carrying adequate insurance to protect its own activities, rather than a requirement imposed on the group alone.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall not indemnify Group and makes no commitment to defend Group against any claim, and Group waives any right to claim indemnification from the Hotel under this Agreement or under applicable law, except as expressly modified by the indemnity limitations set forth herein.
findings.headline: Hotel gives no indemnity; Group waives indemnity rights
findings.finding_text: Protection runs one way only, and the group gives up even indemnification rights it might have under law. The group would bear its own losses from incidents the Hotel causes.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual and limited to each party's own negligence or willful misconduct, including each party's reasonable attorney's fees, and should survive the end of the agreement — the group should never indemnify the hotel for the hotel's own negligence. Insurance should be a mutual obligation, with each party carrying adequate insurance to protect its own activities, rather than a requirement imposed on the group alone.

findings.quoted_text: Group shall maintain comprehensive general liability insurance covering all activities related to the event, with a minimum limit of not less than $5,000,000.00 per occurrence, with the Hotel named as an additional insured.
findings.headline: Group alone must carry $5M liability cover naming the Hotel
findings.finding_text: Insurance is a one-sided duty with a high limit, and the Hotel has no matching obligation. The group's coverage is also made primary over the Hotel's own insurance.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual and limited to each party's own negligence or willful misconduct, including each party's reasonable attorney's fees, and should survive the end of the agreement — the group should never indemnify the hotel for the hotel's own negligence. Insurance should be a mutual obligation, with each party carrying adequate insurance to protect its own activities, rather than a requirement imposed on the group alone.

findings.quoted_text: Group shall provide the Hotel with attendee lists containing names, email addresses, phone numbers, and other registration information in connection with the April 12-16, 2027 event, and Group acknowledges that the Hotel may utilize such attendee data for the Hotel's own marketing, promotional, and business development purposes, including but not limited to direct mail, email marketing, targeted advertising, and future event solicitation directed to attendees or their affiliated organizations.
findings.headline: Hotel may market to attendees using the rooming data
findings.finding_text: Attendee contact details given for reservations can be used for the Hotel's own promotion, and the group consents in advance. The group's members could be solicited without their agreement.
findings.cd_standard: Rooming list and attendee data provided to the hotel for reservation purposes should not be used by the hotel for its own marketing or sold to third parties without the group's consent. This is distinct from CD's own client-confidentiality question but sits in the same family of concerns.

findings.quoted_text: In addition to the Hotel's own use, Group authorizes the Hotel to share and disclose attendee data with the Hotel's corporate affiliates, brand partners, and third-party marketing service providers who assist the Hotel in analyzing market trends, identifying corporate event opportunities, and promoting the Hotel's services and facilities to potential group customers.
findings.headline: Attendee data may be shared with affiliates and marketers
findings.finding_text: Attendee information can pass to affiliates, brand partners and third-party marketers without further notice. The group also waives claims over the Hotel's handling and disclosure of that data.
findings.cd_standard: Rooming list and attendee data provided to the hotel for reservation purposes should not be used by the hotel for its own marketing or sold to third parties without the group's consent. This is distinct from CD's own client-confidentiality question but sits in the same family of concerns.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel makes no representation, warranty, or covenant regarding the accessibility of its facilities under the Americans with Disabilities Act, as amended, or any state or local accessibility law, and Group assumes sole responsibility for assessing the suitability of the Hotel's premises for Group's attendees and event purposes.
findings.headline: Hotel gives no accessibility warranty at all
findings.finding_text: The Hotel disclaims any statement about ADA compliance, leaving the group to verify guest rooms, common areas and function space itself. The group could face attendee claims about facilities it does not control.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should warrant that its guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation services comply with the ADA's public accommodation requirements, with each party indemnifying the other only for its own ADA obligations — and a clear division of who funds auxiliary aids in event space (group) versus guest rooms and common areas (hotel).

findings.quoted_text: Should Group require auxiliary aids, services, modifications, or accommodations to make any portion of the Hotel accessible or usable by Group's attendees, Group shall fund and arrange for all such auxiliary aids and accommodations, including but not limited to interpreters, readers, accessible transportation, specialized signage, or technology enhancements, regardless of where within the Hotel such aids or accommodations are required or how they are deployed.
findings.headline: Group pays for all accessibility aids throughout the Hotel
findings.finding_text: Costs for accommodations in guest rooms and common areas, which are normally the hotel's responsibility, fall on the group. The group's costs are open-ended and the 60-day notice requirement adds further exposure.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should warrant that its guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation services comply with the ADA's public accommodation requirements, with each party indemnifying the other only for its own ADA obligations — and a clear division of who funds auxiliary aids in event space (group) versus guest rooms and common areas (hotel).

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel makes no commitment to any standard, policy, or practice beyond what such applicable law expressly requires, and the Group shall not be entitled to invoke any nondiscrimination clause, covenant, or principle not grounded in enforceable legal requirement.
findings.headline: No nondiscrimination commitment beyond bare legal minimum
findings.finding_text: The Hotel gives no affirmative pledge to treat attendees equally where law would permit otherwise. Attendees could be treated differently in places where the law allows it, with no contractual recourse.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should commit that it and its staff will not discriminate against any attendee on the basis of sex, gender identity or expression, age, race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information, family, marital, or military status, or similar grounds, even where state or federal law would allow it. If the state or city adopts legislation that allows such discrimination or bars local nondiscrimination measures, the group should be able to terminate without liability.

findings.quoted_text: In the event that any change, amendment, or new enactment of state or local law relating to discrimination, equal treatment, or the provision of services occurs after the date of this Agreement and before or during the Event, the Group shall have no right to cancel this Agreement, terminate the group block, reduce the room block commitment, or claim any modification to the terms hereof.
findings.headline: No exit if discriminatory law is enacted
findings.finding_text: If new legislation permits discrimination against attendees, the group must still perform and pay damages if it withdraws. The group's only option is to ask for operational changes at the Hotel's discretion.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should commit that it and its staff will not discriminate against any attendee on the basis of sex, gender identity or expression, age, race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information, family, marital, or military status, or similar grounds, even where state or federal law would allow it. If the state or city adopts legislation that allows such discrimination or bars local nondiscrimination measures, the group should be able to terminate without liability.

findings.quoted_text: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the state in which the Hotel is located, without regard to its conflict of law principles, and the parties irrevocably submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Maryland for the resolution of any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement, the event, or the performance or breach hereof.
findings.headline: Disputes governed by Maryland law in Maryland courts
findings.finding_text: Any dispute must be brought in the Hotel's home forum, raising the group's cost and travel burden. The group also waives objections based on inconvenience.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law and any dispute venue should be the state and city where the group is located, not the hotel's — keeping litigation costs and home-court advantage on the group's side — with no punitive damages and each party bearing its own attorney's fees.

findings.quoted_text: In any action or proceeding brought by the Hotel to enforce its rights or to recover damages for breach of this Agreement, the Hotel shall be entitled to recover, in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity and in addition to any actual damages awarded, an award of punitive damages to the extent permitted by applicable law.
findings.headline: Hotel may recover punitive damages from the group
findings.finding_text: Only the Hotel can seek punitive damages on top of actual damages, so a dispute could cost the group well beyond its real loss.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law and any dispute venue should be the state and city where the group is located, not the hotel's — keeping litigation costs and home-court advantage on the group's side — with no punitive damages and each party bearing its own attorney's fees.

findings.quoted_text: In the event of any dispute, claim, or proceeding arising from or relating to this Agreement, including any action for breach, enforcement, or interpretation, the prevailing party shall be entitled to recover reasonable attorney's fees, court costs, and all other expenses of litigation, including expert fees and investigation costs, from the non-prevailing party as part of the judgment or award. The Hotel shall be deemed the prevailing party if it recovers any material relief, whether by judgment, settlement, or otherwise.
findings.headline: Fee shifting tilted so Hotel is prevailing if it recovers anything
findings.finding_text: The group could pay the Hotel's legal and expert costs after a partial loss, while the definition favors the Hotel. This also conflicts with Section 7, where the group bears its own fees against the Hotel.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law and any dispute venue should be the state and city where the group is located, not the hotel's — keeping litigation costs and home-court advantage on the group's side — with no punitive damages and each party bearing its own attorney's fees.

findings.quoted_text: Group shall be responsible for communicating the cutoff date to all attendees and shall indemnify the Hotel against any claims arising from Group's failure to do so.
findings.headline: Group indemnifies Hotel for claims over Group's use of Hotel name or marks
findings.finding_text: The group must indemnify the Hotel for claims arising from attendees not being told the cutoff date. This is an open-ended liability for an administrative communication task.
findings.cd_standard: Not covered by CD's standards library. Raise it at your discretion.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall calculate all such damages from its books and records and shall provide Group with a detailed accounting upon request. Group shall pay such damages within thirty (30) days of invoice.
findings.headline: Group pays Hotel's own damages when terminating for Hotel's breach
findings.finding_text: Damages are computed solely from the Hotel's own records and invoiced to the group even after the Hotel's breach. The group has no means to challenge the figures.
findings.cd_standard: Not covered by CD's standards library. Raise it at your discretion.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall calculate attrition based on the Hotel's registration records and room records, which constitute the final and binding record of occupancy for purposes of this agreement.
findings.headline: Hotel's records are the final and binding record of occupancy
findings.finding_text: The group cannot contest the occupancy figures that determine attrition liability. Combined with the audit waiver, errors or miscoded rooms would go uncorrected.
findings.cd_standard: Not covered by CD's standards library. Raise it at your discretion.

findings.quoted_text: Failure to pay any shortfall by the due date shall result in late charges at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, compounded monthly, on the outstanding balance.
findings.headline: Compounding 1.5% late charge on F&B shortfall
findings.finding_text: Late charges accrue at 1.5% compounded monthly on any unpaid shortfall, about 19.6% a year, with no dispute carve-out.
findings.cd_standard: Not covered by CD's standards library. Raise it at your discretion.

findings.quoted_text: This deposit shall be held in the Hotel's general operating account and shall not earn interest on behalf of the Group.
findings.headline: Deposit retained and tied to Group even when Hotel fails
findings.finding_text: The $25,000 deposit is held in the Hotel's operating account with no segregation, so it is exposed to the Hotel's creditors or insolvency. The Hotel has no duty to preserve it.
findings.cd_standard: Not covered by CD's standards library. Raise it at your discretion.

clause_review.basis: Requires pricing locked no earlier than 12 months out (contract: 24 months, pricing outside window revisable), shortfall at 35% (contract: 100%), affiliate/exhibitor F&B counting (silent).
Requires freedom to use outside vendors at no fee; contract mandates Hotel-appointed vendors and a $2,500 surcharge per outside vendor.

Requires 1 comp per 40 cumulative rooms (contract: 1 per 75, discretionary guideline), no forfeiture for attrition (contract forfeits below 100% of block), miscoded/no-show/cancel nights counted (silent), free in-room internet for all attendees (silent); also comps charged resort fee/taxes.

Requires all charges disclosed pre-signature and undisclosed waived, written approval for add-ons, resort fee waived, no early check-in/bag fees; contract allows post-signature fees, waives objections, and charges $35 resort fee including on comp rooms.
Requires assignment to successor management/affiliate with consent not unreasonably withheld; contract allows consent withheld in Hotel's absolute discretion for any reason.

Requires notice within 30 days of change, 30-day termination window, refund within 5 days, covers bankruptcy/foreclosure; contract gives notice only 'commercially reasonable efforts' before change, 10-day termination window, no refund, and excludes bankruptcy/foreclosure.

Requires refund within 30 days absent itemized damage and no offset against attrition/F&B/cancellation; contract's $25,000 deposit refunds in 90 days and may be applied to attrition, F&B shortfalls and cancellation.

Requires no-liability termination for force majeure, epidemic, labor dispute, ownership change, renovation, facility reductions, convention center unavailability, discriminatory legislation, separate from cancellation scale; contract allows termination only for uncured material breach and treats all termination as cancellation with damages.

Requires 24/12-month block reviews with adjustment rights (silent), weekly pickup reports (contract: only on request), post-event report within 30 days (contract: 90 days), no-cost room-block audit and miscoded-room credit (contract: no audit rights).
Requires mutual indemnity limited to own negligence and mutual insurance; contract has Group-only indemnity extending to Hotel's own negligence, Hotel gives none, and insurance is Group-only.
Requires no hotel marketing use or third-party sale without consent; contract authorizes marketing use and sharing with affiliates and third parties in advance.

Requires either party cancel without liability on a forecast storm within 72 hours; contract gives Group a right only on 24-hour notice and forfeits the deposit; Baltimore is a hurricane-region market.
Requires CBA expiration notice, dispute notice within 10 working days, and no-liability cancellation within 90 days; contract gives no notice and expressly denies any cancellation right (Section 24).

Requires gratuity (18%) and service charge (6%) separately defined and confirmed, gratuity fully distributed to staff, none on room rental/labor-fee equipment; contract uses one undefined 24% charge interchangeably, retained at Hotel's discretion, applied to room charges.

Requires Hotel warranty of ADA compliance for rooms/common areas/function space/transport, mutual indemnity for own obligations, group funds aids only in event space; contract disclaims all accessibility representation and puts all aids on Group everywhere in the Hotel.

Requires advance contact, do-not-walk list, walk after others, comparable lodging and transport at Hotel's cost, upgrade/amenity, $200 credit, pickup credit, no attrition liability; contract puts all costs on guest, no upgrade, no pickup credit.

Requires payable on receipt with dispute window, finance charge capped at 1%/month, auto-credit if no application, staged deposit schedule if credit denied; contract waives dispute rights, charges 1.5% compounded, prepayment at Hotel's discretion.

Requires affirmative documented resale effort, proceeds credited, damages due 30 days after meeting with evidence, records available; contract disclaims any duty, keeps all proceeds, bars inspection and waives mitigation claims.

Requires named rooms with square footage/ceiling height, no change without mutual written consent, meeting space complimentary with rental waived, basic AV items free; contract assigns at Hotel's discretion, unnamed (Exhibit A names rooms but no sizes, tentative), rental charged, no basics.
Requires Hotel to owe direct, indirect and consequential damages and fees on unauthorized cancellation; contract limits remedy to deposit refund, excludes consequential damages and waives fees.
Rates are fixed at $289 for the April 2027 event; contract does not leave future-year rates unconfirmed.
Requires cutoff 21 days or fewer before arrival (contract: 45 days), post-cutoff group rate while Hotel sells to public (contract: rack rate only), handling of unassigned rooms (silent).

Requires confirmations within 4 days, name changes at group rate, free cancellation until 6 pm arrival day, no-show reinstated next night, refundable deposits, cancellation money credited against attrition; contract reprices name changes, cancels full stay on first-night no-show, requires 72 hours' notice, and credits nothing.

Requires sliding scale on 70% of net rate x block less attrition with dollar amounts shown, mitigation credit, rebook credit, actual damages only; contract uses gross room revenue on full block, percentages only, no resale credit, no rebook credit.
Requires affirmative commitment beyond legal minimum and no-liability termination if discriminatory legislation adopted; contract limits to legal requirements and denies any cancellation right.
Requires alternatives at Hotel's expense for facility/service reductions over 25% and cancellation right if no agreement in 30 days; contract is silent.

Requires no-renovation representation, 30 days' notice with scope/schedule/mitigation, no-liability termination if interference; contract disclaims everything, requires no notice and denies termination or remedies.

Requires cumulative measurement (contract: night-by-night), 70% trigger (contract: 90%), 70% of rate on unsold rooms only (contract: 100% of rate), 95% occupancy night credit (contract: only sell-out nights deemed satisfied, no credit), audit rights (contract: waived), F&B/rebook credits (silent).
Requires 10% commission to ConferenceDirect on all actualized room revenue within 30 days of departure plus related protections; contract is silent on commission.

Requires cancellation without liability when performance is illegal/impossible/impracticable/inadvisable or 20% attendee cancellations, with terrorism, disease, travel advisories, government closures included, deposits refunded; contract limits to physical impossibility, excludes epidemics and government restrictions, retains deposits, 48-hour notice.
Requires law/venue in Group's home state, no punitive damages, each party bears own fees; contract uses Maryland law/courts, punitive damages for Hotel, and prevailing-party fees favoring Hotel.

Requires rate matched including retroactively with commission and pickup credit kept, and no higher than other groups within 7 days; contract bars retroactive adjustment, makes adjusted rate non-commissionable and excluded from pickup, and is silent on other groups' rates.

Requires minimum server/bartender ratios with no labor fees except functions under 25 people ($150); contract leaves staffing to Hotel discretion and charges labor and bartender fees on all functions.

Requires honored AV/internet quotes, 10/1 Mbps minimum, 20% discount on additions, and no in-house AV condition for complimentary services; contract denies quoted pricing, gives no bandwidth or discount, and conditions complimentary internet on exclusive in-house AV.

document_notes.headline: Attrition formula multiplies occupied rooms, not unoccupied rooms.
document_notes.detail: Section 2 says damages are for 'each unoccupied room' but then 'multiplying the nightly room rate by the number of occupied rooms'. The two sentences describe different calculations.

document_notes.headline: Fee-shifting terms conflict between Sections 7 and 32.
